prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the vertical layout of an indoor construction space with multi-tier bamboo scaffolding as the camera wearer pitches their head from looking upward (frames 1–2), sharply downward to the floor (frame 3), across mid-level poles (frame 4), and back upward (frame 5). In frames 1, 2, and 5, bright foreground values place the lower scaffolding poles and a plastering trowel within or near the camera wearer's arm's reach at 0.5–1.5 m below and in front, while above them a partially cropped worker on the right stands at ~2–2.5 m (facing left/away) and a second worker stands ~1.5–2 m further back and to the left on upper poles at ~3.5–4.5 m (facing right and looking downward in frames 1–2, then upward with a brick within his overhead reach in frame 5). As the camera tilts down in frame 3, the map shows a rectangular bucket and round pans on the floor ~1–2.5 m below (with the nearest container and poles close to arm's reach), before tilting up in frame 4 to show horizontal scaffolding ~1–2 m ahead. Crucially, the depth map reveals the full 3D geometry of the mid-level bamboo poles and the faint silhouette of the distant standing worker (~3.5–4 m above) in the severely underexposed frame 4 that are nearly invisible in RGB alone. However, it is unreliable where it completely misses the mid-air block near the distant worker's reach in frame 2, merges narrow gaps between adjacent bamboo poles, and misinterprets flat floor shadows and dark basins in frame 3 as distinct depth surfaces.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates only human figures against a black background, omitting the room walls, bamboo scaffolding, floor containers, and bricks across all five frames. In frames 1 and 2, it identifies the distant worker standing above and to the left (~3.5–4.5 m from the camera wearer, facing right and looking down toward the camera wearer's direction with his arms in front within reach of a brick) and the nearer worker ~1.5–2 m to his right (~2–2.5 m from the camera wearer, facing away/left with his right side and upper body partially occluded by the right frame edge). As the camera wearer turns their head sharply downward in frame 3, upward through the dark mid-section in frame 4, and back to the upper scaffolding in frame 5, the two workers exit and re-enter the field of view while remaining on their respective perches. The masks make it easy to separate the foreground right-side worker's silhouette from the background wall in frames 1–2, but the map is highly unreliable overall. It swaps instance colours between the two workers from frame 1 to frame 2, falsely labels the camera wearer's flat ground shadow and an adjacent round pan (~1.5–2 m below) as a person in frame 3, and completely fails to detect the distant worker reaching overhead and the right-side worker's lower leg in frames 4 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders sparse 2D yellow body skeletons on a black background without any scene geometry, objects, or closer foreground figures. It detects the distant worker standing on the upper-left scaffolding (~3.5–4.5 m away and above the camera wearer, ~1.5–2 m left of the nearer worker) only in frames 2 and 5, showing him facing right and looking downward toward the camera wearer/right in frame 2, and turning his head and both raised arms upward within reach of an airborne brick in frame 5. Across the sequence, as the camera pitches down in frame 3, up through the dark scaffolding in frame 4, and back to the ceiling in frame 5, the map tracks the distant worker's transition from a lowered-arm stance to an overhead catch posture. In frame 5, the yellow skeletal links clearly isolate the exact angles of the distant worker's raised elbows and wrists against the dim ceiling, which are harder to parse in RGB. However, the map is unreliable because it misses the distant worker in frames 1 and 4, completely misses the partially cropped worker on the right (~2–2.5 m away) in frames 1, 2, and 5, detects no magenta hand skeletons for anyone, and hallucinates a torso-and-head skeleton onto the camera wearer's 2D shadow on the floor (~1.5–2 m below) in frame 3.
